10:54 PM
We actually have a completely useless section of the code now that I think about it
10:59 PM
New York is one of 33 states with fault based divorce on its books, meaning you can plead adultery, cruelty, abandonment, imprisonment or substance abuse and have to prove that in court to get a divorce. However, every state in the US is also a no-fault divorce state, where you just plead irreconcilable differences aka "I don't want to be married anymore, please give me a divorce." No-fault essentially renders at-fault useless as no-fault is absurdly more easy to prove in court. I know lawyers that have been doing this for 30-40 years and have never done an at-fault divorce. At-fault laws are genuinely useless but no one has bothered to remove them from our law
11:03 PM
Another quirk is we place sentimental value very highly when discussing division of personal property. There are cases out there where spouses argue over the possession of beanie babies and crocs. Also, if a spouse received an advanced degree like a law degree or a doctorate, that degree is subject to division in divorce entitling the spouse without the degree to a cut of their ex's potential earning capacity
